subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 39-year-old woman is evaluated for fatigue, cold intolerance, and 6 kg of weight gain. She has dry skin and a firm, mildly enlarged thyroid gland. TSH is 18 mIU/L, free T4 is low, total cholesterol is 312 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol is 218 mg/dL, and triglycerides are normal. Her diet contains little saturated fat.
question: Which of the following best explains the elevated LDL cholesterol in this patient?

options.text: Reduced thyroxine stimulation of hepatic HMG-CoA reductase and LDL receptor expression
Increased hepatic VLDL secretion caused by insulin resistance
A defective apo B-100 that cannot bind the LDL receptor
Impaired intestinal absorption of bile acids

explanation_correct: Thyroxine stimulates HMG-CoA reductase and also increases hepatic LDL receptor expression, so hypothyroidism both raises cholesterol synthesis and reduces LDL clearance. This produces a secondary hypercholesterolemia that resolves when thyroid hormone is replaced and LDL receptor activity is restored.

explanation_incorrect.B: Insulin resistance raises plasma triglycerides through VLDL overproduction, but it does not produce an isolated marked elevation of LDL cholesterol.
explanation_incorrect.C: Lipoprotein lipase deficiency raises triglycerides and chylomicrons dramatically while LDL cholesterol is not the predominant abnormality.
explanation_incorrect.D: A defective apo B-100 is the cause of the inherited disorder familial hypercholesterolemia, which would not be accompanied by the thyroid abnormalities described.
explanation_incorrect.E: Impaired bile acid absorption lowers, rather than raises, plasma cholesterol because hepatic cholesterol is diverted into bile acid synthesis.

educationalObjective: Hypothyroidism causes secondary hypercholesterolemia because thyroxine normally stimulates HMG-CoA reductase and hepatic LDL receptor expression.
